environment: This is a deterministic in-memory Node.js model of discrete ticks and request admission, not a live load balancer or network stack. Predict before running; we can run it after your answer.

cases.surface: bounded worker with an unbounded queue under sustained overload (2 arrivals/tick, 1 completion/tick)
cases.question: Predict every printed line. Explain why completed stays bounded at 1/tick while queuedAtTick5 grows and wait latency rises.

criteria.description: Predicts completed:5, queuedAtTick5:5, maxQueueDepth:5, and latencies:[1,2,2,3,3].
Explains that a queue buffers bursts without adding completion capacity, so sustained arrival above service rate grows queue depth and wait time.

wrongModels.claim: Adding an unbounded queue lets the worker drain all 10 requests in 5 ticks.

cases.surface: bounded queue (maxQueue=2) rejecting excess arrivals under the same 2-vs-1 overload
cases.question: Predict every printed line. Contrast how bounded shedding caps queue depth and latency versus the unbounded queue.

criteria.description: Predicts completed:5, rejected:4, queuedAtTick5:1, and maxLatency:2.
Explains that explicit rejection trades dropped excess requests for bounded backlog and capped wait time instead of unbounded queue growth.

wrongModels.claim: Rejecting excess arrivals reduces completed work below the service capacity per tick.

cases.surface: timed-out queued requests retrying once against a saturated single-tick worker
cases.question: Predict every printed line. Explain how retries under saturation amplify admitted load even when service rate is unchanged.

criteria.description: Predicts admitted:5, completed:4, timedOutAndRetried:1, and remainingQueued:1.
Explains that retrying queued/slow work injects extra demand into an already saturated bottleneck, increasing admitted load without creating capacity.

wrongModels.claim: Retries clear the backlog faster because retried requests get served ahead of new arrivals.
